---
title: "How I Work"
subtitle: "The standard every project on this site is held to."
toc: true
---

An analysis is useful to a commander when it is right, and when the person briefing it
can say how far it goes. These are the practices behind the work on this site.

## Every number has a receipt

Each figure on this site traces to a script, a log, or a saved artifact in the project's
repository. Run manifests record the commit, the parameters, and the library versions, so
any table can be traced back to the code that produced it.

## Evaluate on data the model never saw

Performance is reported on held-out data, split the way the model will be used: by time
when the future is what matters, by unit or person when the model has to generalize to new
ones. Training-time scores are diagnostics, not results.

## Compare against something

A number without a baseline is not a finding. The naive alternative goes next to the
model: the majority class, last year's rate, a random policy, the current manual process.

## Report uncertainty with the estimate

Win rates come with game counts and intervals. Model scores come with variation across
seeds or folds. Simulation output comes with the number of replications behind it, and
with variance reduction where the design allows it.

## Don't test the hypothesis on the data that suggested it

Selecting variables and then testing them on the same rows manufactures significance.
When a method selects, the inference happens on separate data or with a correction built
for selection.

## Verify the engine before trusting the experiment

Simulations get conformance tests, seeded replay determinism, and convergence checks on
the discretization. An experiment is only as good as the engine underneath it, so the
engine gets tested like software, not assumed like a formula.

## Say what the analysis covers

Every model has a boundary: the data it was fit on, the assumptions carrying the result,
the conditions under which it would not hold. Stating that boundary is what makes the
result usable by someone who has to act on it.
